summary: Inserts string a2 into a unique string linked list if it is not already present. Traverses from the head, comparing a2 against each node's string (falling back to global byte_5EA438 when a node has no string) via sub_588410; on a match it returns without inserting. When no match is found it allocates an 8-byte string node and a 12-byte list node, links the list node onto the tail (or makes it the head when the list is empty), updates head/cursor/tail and increments the node count.

operations.description: Guard: if the input string a2 is null the function returns immediately with no insertion.
Traversal cursor this[12] (offset 0x30) is initialized to the head this[10] (offset 0x28).
Guard: traversal starts only when the head (this+0x28) is non-null and its first node is non-null; otherwise the function jumps straight to insertion.
Loop walks the list from the head node; each iteration compares the current node's string to a2.
Read the current node's string pointer; when it is null, global byte_5EA438 is used as the comparison string.
sub_588410 compares a2 against the node string; a zero result means the strings match.
Guard: on a string match (sub_588410 returns 0) the traversal breaks and no duplicate is inserted.
Advance the traversal: cursor this[12] moves to the next node stored at cursor + 4; the loop continues while the next node is non-null.
OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper allocates an 8-byte string node for a2.
Initialize the 8-byte string node: dword[0] set to 0 and dword[1] set to -1.
StringCopyWithBufferRealloc copies a2 into the allocated 8-byte string node buffer.
Initialize the 12-byte list node: dword[0] points to the string node, dword[1] (next) is 0, and byte[8] is 1.
Guard: if the head (this+0x28) is non-null the new node is appended to the tail (this+0x2C); otherwise it becomes the head and the cursor.
Tail this[11] (offset 0x2C) is set to the new node and the node count this[13] (offset 0x34) is incremented.
Void return; every path (null input, duplicate match, or insertion) reaches the end.
